title.narrative: Contributing to conflict transformation and social cohesion in the hills around Bujumbura (Burundi)

description.narrative: The lack of transparency in the electoral process and absence of political agreement between major’s actors in Burundi in leading of public life has triggered violent protests by opponents, what motivated the international community to launch the initiatives to reactivate the dialogue amongst stakeholders to allay the overall situation within the country. The security situation across Burundi remains volatile and church leaders called to quickly engage an inclusive dialogue for decanting political situation. Burundian major donors withdraw for lack of democracy and human rights abuses within the country by rolling party The project seeks to address the issue of social cohesion between displaced, demobilized, returnees and residents in the hills around Bujumbura in Burundi. These groups were separated during the war faced by Burundian in 1993 and were people were killed on ethnic basis. This project includes activities aimed to reinforce relationships and build mutual trust between these groups through consolidating SILC (saving and internal lending communities) mechanisms. Project plans to implement 36 SILCS consisting of 25 persons each living together in the hills. CDJP will not fund the SILCs’ capital start up. The initial capital will be granted by contributions from SILCs members. The project is planning to grant small premiums for field officers who will be responsible for the supervision of these SILCS. One Internal Micro credit expert will support SILCs management. SILCs members will set a credit union that will be fuelled by contributions from members. After making contributions, they will proceed to the distribution of small credits to those who need them at an agreed interest rate in the group. SILC’s meeting planned will also be an opportunity to discuss the challenges of cohabitation in the hills and therefore an opportunity to peaceful manage conflicts. Project aims to focus on these common economic interests for beneficiaries that will promote collaboration, understanding, peaceful coexistence and even reconciliation. The activities included in this project will be carried out in the Archdiocese of Bujumbura. However, in order to be more efficient and efficient, and since our area of intervention is large, the CDJP Bujumbura will consolidate SILC experience in four parishes including RUSHUBI, MUNANIRA, KIVOGA and MURAMVYA as a new parish.
